meetings.headline: Committee declined to weigh in on the track article, kept the senior center network project, and set meetings for Nov 19 and Nov 30.

meetings.headline: Capital Planning Committee unanimously recommends the FY27 capital plan, which needs a two-thirds town meeting vote
meetings.summary: The committee heard the town manager present the final FY27 capital program and its funding mix, discussed the two-thirds vote required because of stabilization-fund use and how a failed vote could be handled, then voted unanimously to recommend approval as presented. Members also debated the town's reliance on free cash versus taxation for capital and future big-ticket purchases, and discussed the unresolved track-and-field engineering issue likely to return at a special town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Taxation (raise and appropriate) funding for capital
budget_items.what_was_said: This year's taxation contribution to the capital plan is the same as last year's; prior years it was zero, and ARPA funds covered FY25.
The town manager recommended funding the plan from free cash, from taxation at the same level as before, and from the special purpose stabilization fund.
The fund was started in 2017 for vehicle and equipment capital needs, requires a two-thirds vote to use, and its current balance was stated.
A member noted the town is deferring purchases of six-wheel dump trucks that will need financing in the near future.
A member estimated an amount of free cash would be left on the table after the planned motions pass, and discussed whether to leave it as free cash or move it to stabilization.
Two separate warrant articles would appropriate free cash to stabilization funds: one to the general purpose stabilization fund and one to the health insurance special purpose stabilization fund.
The chair estimated the price tag for engineering and planning work on the track and field project, expected to come before a special town meeting.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee voted unanimously to recommend the FY27 capital plan as presented, which needs a two-thirds vote at town meeting.
The plan draws on free cash, taxation at the prior level, and the special purpose stabilization fund, and using that fund is what triggers the two-thirds threshold.
Members raised what happens if the two-thirds vote fails at town meeting; the chair will discuss that contingency with the town moderator beforehand.
An unresolved cost for engineering and planning on the track and field project is expected to come back at a special town meeting.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked for a two-thirds vote on the FY27 capital plan at town meeting because it uses the special purpose stabilization fund, a higher bar than a routine appropriation.
The mix of free cash, taxation, and stabilization funding for vehicles and equipment affects how future large purchases, like dump trucks members flagged for FY28-29, get financed.
A separate track and field engineering cost is unresolved and likely heads to a special town meeting, a second vote residents should expect.
